principles: Never run Python-level attribute reads/writes, str(), repr(), __name__ or isinstance on a foreign (callback-supplied) object outside a BaseException guard; use interpreter-level non-overridable accessors where they exist.
The propagating exception object is always the original one: optional bookkeeping (formatting, attachment, journaling) can fail but can never replace or swallow the propagating exception.

Every exception the module observes stays retained: in the propagating object's interpreter-set context chain and, where the module keeps a journal or log, as bounded descriptions of the whole chain. A bookkeeping failure is itself recorded as a fixed marker wherever a record still exists.
